sourceCopy.examplesHeading: Four labels, four useful starting points

examples.heading: An internal stock label
examples.text: UV-2026-001 stays UV-2026-001 in Code 128. Letters, digits and hyphens can share one reference.

examples.heading: Add a missing check digit
examples.text: The documented example 941234554321 becomes 9412345543219 in EAN-13. Its final digit is 9.

examples.heading: Keep the leading zero
examples.text: UPC-A input 01234567890 becomes 012345678905. The first zero remains part of the encoded identifier.

examples.heading: A shorter retail symbol
examples.text: EAN-8 input 1234567 becomes 12345670. A shorter format does not grant a valid product allocation.

method.heading: A readable barcode starts with the right data
paragraphs: A barcode represents an identifier. It does not register a product, create ownership or prove that a retailer accepts the number. Use an allocated identifier when your retailer requires one. The sample numbers demonstrate arithmetic; they are not offered for commercial allocation.

EAN-13, UPC-A and EAN-8 use a final check digit. Starting at the rightmost data digit, multiply alternate digits by three. Add the remaining digits. Choose the smallest final digit that brings that sum to a multiple of ten. A sum already divisible by ten needs zero.

Enter the data digits alone to calculate the final digit. Enter a complete number to validate it. The generator rejects a wrong supplied digit. It never repairs a complete product number without telling you. Leading zeroes remain strings throughout the calculation.

Code 128 accepts printable ASCII characters. It can switch between character sets to encode a reference efficiently. This page generates ordinary Code 128, not GS1-128 with application identifiers or FNC1. Code 39 accepts its smaller uppercase alphabet. Its optional Modulo-43 checksum is not added here.

Bars remain black on a solid white background in both themes. The image reserves twelve narrow-bar widths of clear space at each side. Do not crop those margins, stretch only one dimension or place text across the bars. Colour choices that reduce contrast are deliberately absent.

SVG keeps exact bar positions at any scale. PNG is a raster image at the selected pixel size. Printed dimensions, ink spread, paper, scanner settings and print quality still affect reading. Our pixel controls do not certify compliance with a physical retail specification. Test the final label at its intended size.

uses.heading: One label or a repeatable list
paragraphs: Use Code 128 for stock references, order numbers or shelf labels in your own system. Confirm the receiving scanner supports the selected format. Use EAN or UPC when an allocated retail number and the receiving system require that format.

A list uses one format and size for every line. Empty lines are skipped; spaces in Code 128 remain meaningful data. The ZIP gives each valid row a numbered SVG filename. The CSV manifest preserves the original line, input, encoded value and any error. Duplicate input lines intentionally produce matching barcodes.

The list runs in a background worker. You can cancel it before the complete archive is ready. The page shows only five valid previews to keep the interface light. That display choice does not remove other valid images from the ZIP.

There is no daily generation quota or eighty-character cap. Long Code 128 values create wide images. Your browser and device memory determine what fits. If PNG cannot handle a very wide canvas, download SVG or use shorter identifiers that suit your real scanner.

privacy.heading: Your identifiers stay with you
paragraphs: Generation, check digits, SVG, PNG and ZIP creation happen on your device. No barcode service receives the input. Calculations work without a network after the page has loaded.

The page does not save your input in browser storage. A copied share link contains the value and size options. Share it only when the identifier may be seen by others. Batch inputs are excluded from share links.

Downloads contain your identifiers. Check the destination folder before sharing an archive. CSV values that look like spreadsheet formulas receive a leading apostrophe for safer opening. This changes the manifest cell, not the actual encoded identifier.

faq.question: Is this barcode generator free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, daily quota or payment step. Generation and downloads run in your browser.

faq.question: Which barcode formats can I create?
faq.answer: Code 128, EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8 and Code 39. Choose the format required by the system that reads the label.

faq.question: Can this assign a retail product number?
faq.answer: No. It draws an identifier that you supply. A valid check digit does not prove a number is allocated to you.

faq.question: Why is my check digit rejected?
faq.answer: The final digit does not match the preceding digits. Check the original identifier. Entering data digits alone calculates a missing digit.

faq.question: Will leading zeroes disappear?
faq.answer: No. Retail inputs stay as strings, and each leading zero remains in the normalized value and barcode.

faq.question: Is Code 128 the same as GS1-128?
faq.answer: No. This page makes ordinary Code 128. It does not insert FNC1 or validate GS1 application identifiers.

faq.question: Should I download SVG or PNG?
faq.answer: Choose SVG for scaling and label design. PNG is convenient for image software. Preserve the white margins and test the final print.

faq.question: Can I create a batch without a row limit?
faq.answer: Yes, within your device memory. Each valid line gets an SVG in the ZIP. The CSV manifest lists every processed line and error.

faq.question: Why is a long barcode wider than the preview?
faq.answer: Every character needs bars and spaces. The preview scrolls to preserve the bar width. The downloaded SVG keeps the full image.

faq.question: Does a successful screen scan certify a printed label?
faq.answer: No. Paper, printer, size and scanner conditions affect reading. Test your actual label and obtain formal verification when required.
